title: Update class member handling
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

The intent of this PR is to streamline the logic for parsing member statements for classes, and to make it then easier to fix other issues. This PR includes:

- fixes around comments
- properly handling different scenarios around generics
- initial work to not show members box if there are no attributes or methods
- handle leading newlines
- changed name from "member" to "attribute" to be explicit and distinct from members as a whole

- resolves #3287 
- resolves #1645
- resolves #3189
- resolves #3243 
- partial #2185 

## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions

Added a new class for members specifically, and all parsing of that member is handled within the class itself. Created a more thorough regex specific for methods to capture any of the expected values - or have an empty result if that value was not matched.  There has been talk about whether or not the type or name of an attribute or method parameter should go first - so handling is set to take however the value is typed for that section

comments.author: jakraft
comments.body:
@jgreywolf I don't think it necessarily requires a breaking change. Backward compatibility with the existing "~" format can be retained, but a new syntax is required to add support for multiple generics. The easiest approach I can see is to add support for angle brackets directly ("<>"). This would be fairly trivial to do, it would just require replacing any instances of `<` and `>` with `<` and `>` respectively. This can be done at the top of the parseGenericTypes function before handling the ~ logic.

Is there any reason the recursive call can't be removed regardless? I can't really see a reason to keep it in there.

comments.body: Please see updated code and resolve if acceptable ;)  It does get rid of the max call size issue, and accounts for a couple of edge cases - if more "edge" cases develop this entire solution will have to be revisited.

comments.author: jakraft
comments.body:
This regex will fail if you have more than 1 method parameter using generics. For example:

`Dictionary~Foo, Bar~, Wiz~Bang~` becomes `Dictionary<Foo, Bar<, Wiz>Bang>` when it should instead result in `Dictionary<Foo, Bar>, Wiz<Bang>`

That's the main reason I mentioned there's too much ambiguity using tildes as the syntax since there's not enough information to resolve whether this is 1 parameter or 2. (see #4555)

comments.author: jgreywolf
comments.body:
I see that now. Added a test for that specific scenario.

The problem I see now is - we have been using ~~ to indicate a generic for a couple of years, and to change that would be breaking. Though I am willing to look at doing that, if we go into it with that understanding :)

I was thinking of having the code go through and keep track of where it is in the "parsing".  So that it would know if it had already processed a beginning or end bracket - but you need to be able to account for nested generics

Im open to other suggestions

comments.author: jakraft
comments.body:
Yeah I thought about that, but the issue, like you mentioned, is that even if you scan from left to right, it's impossible to correctly pair up the matching ~~ without guessing. That's why using asymmetric tokens (e.g. <>, [], (), or {}) would be best.

The easiest way to facilitate that would be to replace any instance of <> with HTML-escaped angle brackets (`<` and `>`). This could be added as an alternative syntax without needing to remove support for the legacy tilde syntax and would unblock users wanting to take advantage of more complex generics.

comments.author: jgreywolf
comments.body:
What I was working on today was going right to left.
Count how many tokens (~) there are, divide that by two (rounded down) to determine how many "sets" there are - assuming that if there is an odd number of tokens it would be the first one, and we will skip it.

Keeping track of which "set" we are in, and how many tokens are left, we can figure out if we want > or <.

This has not been nearly as clean as I thought - and I am going to scrap it, I think

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
It might be cleaner to use a [template strings](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Template_literals) here.

```suggestion
      displayText += `(${parseGenericTypes(this.parameters.trim())})`;
```

This is probably a discussion for another time, but there's also an eslint rule called [`prefer-template`](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/rules/prefer-template) that we could enable, then we could use `eslint --fix` to automatically update them, if everybody prefers template strings over string concatenation.
